cells.remarks: VIII, p. 163 The plates are five in number and secured by Chilkuri Narayana Rao, teacher, Srikakulam along with other five sets of C. P. grants. It is a grant made by Mahāraja Vajrahastadeva of the Gaṅga dynasty in Śaka 97 [1], Karkaṭaka, Śakla-paksha, Trayodaśi, Sunday. It records the gift of the village Sattivāḍa in Erada-Vishaya to Gaṇapati Nāyaka, the grandson of Gaṇapati, a resident of the village Valutavuru in Kāñchideśa. [After the Praśasti shown in Appx I.A.] 1. This inscription records the date as “अजगिरिनिधिशाकान्दे कवर्कटमासि शुक्लपत्त्र लयोदस्यामादित्वारे”. If the word Aja is taken as the number I, गिरि-7 and निधि-9, then it will be aka 971, and the corresponding Christian date will be the 16th. July, 1049 A.D. But, on that day the tithi लयोदशी is passed. If the word ‘Aja’ will be either 4 or 7, then the estronomical combination will fit to the corresponding dates i. e. 12-7-1052 and 19-7-1055 A.C. respectively

Ll. 42-71:- ..... कल्ङ्कनगरात् परममाहेश्वरं परमभट्टारक महाराजाधिराज त्रिकल्ङ्काथिपति श्रीमद्‌वज्रहस्तदेव कुशली [॥] समस्तामात्य प्रमुख जनपदान् समाहूय समाज्ञापयति विदितमस्तु भवतां परद विपये सत्तिग्राहां चतुः सीमावच्छिन्नं सज्जलस्थलं सर्व्वपीडा विवर्ज्जितं आचंद्रावर्कं जिति समकालं यावन्मातापित्रोरात्मनः पुण्ययशोवृद्धये अजगिरिनिधिशाकान्दे कवर्कटक मासि शुक्लपत्त्र त्रयोदृश्यामादित्यवारे 1 काञ्चिदेश बलुववुरु ग्रामनिवासिनः गणपत्याख्यस्य मूनः कूनाडिनायकः तस्य भार्य्या श्रीदेवि तयोः संज्जाताय गणपति नायकाय उदकपूर्व्व (र्वर्क) ताम्र(घ्र) शासनं कृत्वा सत्तिवाडां 2 प्रदत्तं [॥] अस्माभिर्भ्राविभिर्भूमिपालै म्मर्नुनो धर्मगौरवात् परिपालनीयमिति [॥] तस्यैव ग्रामस्य सीमा लिख्यन्ते [॥] पूर्व्वस्यां दिशि क्रोप्पल्लिप्राम तटाकान्तर्गतं वन्धोपरि तिन्त्रिणीवृत्तः इन्द्रानेययोर्मध्ये धन्वाकार वक्रं आनेय्यां दिशि तिन्त्रिणी वृत्तः दक्षिणस्यां दिशि त्रिकूट आम्म्र वृत्त वाल्मिकौ नैच्छत्यां दिशि त्रिकूटे वाल्मीक युगलं पञ्चिमस्यां दिशि तिन्त्रिणी वाल्मीकौ वायव्यां
दिशि पाषाणः उत्तरस्यां दिशि त्रिकूटे विषवृक्ष समूहं इशान्यां दिशि त्रिकूटे क्रोष्पलि तटाक व'धोपरि तिंत्रिणी वृक्षः [॥] षष्ठिवर्षं सहस्राणि स्वर्गे मोदति भूमिदः । आक्षेप्ता चानुमंता च तान्येव नरके वसेत् [॥] दत्तमिष्टं तपस्तप्तं हुतं चैव युधिष्ठिर अर्द्धांगुलेन सीमाय(या) हरणेन प्रणइयति [॥] स्वदत्तां परदत्तां वा यो हरेत वसुन्धरां स विष्टायां कृमिभूत्या पितृभिस्सह पत्र्यति( ते )[॥] भूमि यः प्रतिगृह्णाति यश्च भूमिं प्रयज्जति उभौ तौ पुण्य कर्माणौ नियतं स्वर्गं गामिनौ [॥] महाकायस्थ सन्धिविगृहि मावुराय सूनुना सन्धिविगृहि श्री दामोदरेण लिखितं उत्कीरितं अक्षशालि 3 घर्लेमोजुना इति (॥)
cells.notes:
2. The village सल्तिवाडा may be identified with the modern village of साथिवाडा near टिकालि in the Srikakulam District.
3. It seams that 'अक्षशालिन्' is the designation which corresponds to 'अक्षपटल'. According to Monahan, the Akshapaṭala was in charge of both accounts office and record-room (vide Early History of Bengal . p. 45)

cells.text_original: Ll. 44-57:— कलिङ्गनगरात् परममाहेश्वर परमभट्टारक महाराजाधिराज त्रिकलिङ्गाधि-पतिश्रीमद्‌षज्ञहस्तदेव[:] कुशली[||] समस्तामात्यप्रमूखजनपदान् समाहूय समाज्ञापयति [||] त्रिदितमस्तु भवताम् एतद्‌विषये || 1 चिल्‌पुर ग्राममर्गात् स्मन्ना वण्ठुडांमावह्लुरमा अर्णर्गो... लक्ष्मी क्षाकानुरना वोटुरुवाडां, मुरिंगा कनम रम्प 2 हिवरे मचि कीडमा गुदपी एतान् द्वादश ग्रामान् विल्पुर विषये त्रम्मेकीकृत्य चतुःसीमावच्छिन्नः सजलस्थलः सर्वपीडाविवर्जितः आचन्द्राकर् क्षितिसमकालं यावन्मातापित्रो रात्मनश्च पुण्याभिवृद्धये अजगिरिनिधि शाक्राव्दे फौल्गुनामलपक्षे द्वादश्यामादित्यवारे 3 च्छिलि निवासिनः अहतिकाल्य पुत्रः श्रीकण्ठनायकः तस्य माग्यां वेदवी । तयोः संजाताय तांगुसामयाय ताम्रशासनं कृत्या विल्पुरा विषयः प्रदत्तः । कौलि वर्त्तनी विषये नुगिल ग्रामः प्रदत्तः || 4
cells.notes:
1. The black typed portion contains the names of twelve villages which formed the Velpura-Vishaya. It is not possible to distinguish each name of these villages for want of puntuation mark.
2. The name of this village is still in vogue in the ex-Parlakimedi Zamindari.
3. The corresponding Christian date is the 8th. February, 1058 A. D.

cells.king: Vajrahastadeva § 982 (?)
cells.date: 27th Sept. 1059 A. D.
cells.reference: Noticed in A. R. No. 5 for 1924-5; E. I. XXI, I. N. I. No. 1252; Sept. North India type; Lng. Snsk.
cells.object: Chikkalavalasa copperplate grant of Vajrahastadeva § 982 (?)
cells.remarks: Ed. by M. Somasekbara Sarma in “ The Bharati ” (Telugu journal of Madras), Vol. II, pt. ii, p. 138-57.) It is noticed in A.R.No. 5 of 1924-25 and in Bhandarkar's Inscriptions of Northern India, No. 1952. The plates were discovered in a cultivated field lying between Kambakaya and Chikkalavalasa villages in Srikakulam District. The number of the plates is five being attached to a ring where the seal is found. The emblem of a lying bull, the moon, the sun, a conch-shell, a plough and a Chamara are found on the seal. Text [After the praśasti as given in Appendix I-A] I. The date is not regular. But, if it would have been ३ 98r, then the corresponding date would be the 27th Sept. 1059 A. D. and that would also be the day of Tula संक्रान्ति, an auspecious moment for granting दानम्. 'प्रथम पक्ष' refers to the dark fortnight. It shows that the system of श्रमान्त was followed. In addition to the above professions Manu says that a वैश्य should know accountaney:- For these qualifications a वैश्य was usually appointed as the royal treasurer or record-keeper. Then he possessed the titles of श्री करण . etc. 5. The annual payment of rent for the village is 100 मरु or मुरा of paddy and 8 माड़ of coin. The words मुरक and मुरय are also used in some inscriptions of Kaliṅga (vide J.B.O.R.S. vol. XVIII, p. 272; J.A.H.R.S. vol. VIII, p. 168 and E. I. IX, p. 96). It was used as a particular grain measuring unit, which was in vogue in Kaliṅga in the 10th and 11th centuries A. D. I think, this word is still used in Ganjam by the Oriyas as मरेयि. It is a big basket, made of bamboo, for preservation of paddy. Generally a मरेयि holds about one cart-load of paddy, which varies from twelve to fifteen monds. According to Monier William's Sanskrit-English Dictionary the word मुर denotes encampass, entwine, bind together . So मुरा may be equal to a पुडुग or पुड़ा where the paddy is also preserved. Generally a पुडुग contains six monds of paddy, being tied into ropes made of straw. If one मुरा is equal to 12 monds, then the payment of annual rent to the king will be equal to 1200 monds; otherwise it will be half of that amount. It is also interesting to note here that according to the following quotation from धर्मशास्त्र, one sixth part of the total income of a village should be paid to the king. So, the total produce from this village might be either (1200×6=) 7,200 monds or (600×6=) 3,600 monds:- It is not out of place to mention here that in the Kama-Nalinakshapur plates of Jayavarmadeva of the Gaṅga family of Kaliṅga, mention is made of 'मुरज' as a land measuring unit. (O H.'R.'J. Vol. VII, No. 2, p. 84). Probably, the word मुरज was subsequently converted into मुरय and मुर, and at present into मरेयि in the Oriya language

Ll:—38-56 “ .... कलङ्कनगरात् परममाहेश्वर परमभट्टारक महाराजाधिराज त्रिकलिङ्गाधिपति श्रीमदनन्तशर्म वज्रहस्तदेव: कुशली[॥] समस्तामात्प्रमुखजनपदान्समाहूय समाज्ञापयति विदितमस्तु भयतां । कोलुवर्त्त(र्ति)नि विषये ॥ कुद्दमाख्यग्राम: सीमावच्छिन्न: सजलस्थल: सर्व पीड़ायर्जितमाचन्द्राक्कर्षितिसमकाल यावन्मातापित्रोरात्मन: पुण्ययशोभि-वृद्धये । करवसुनिधिशाकाव्दे । कार्तिकमास प्रथमपक्ष तृती[य]यां सो[म]वारे 1 (1) दत्त[म]गोत्रस्य
वैस्य(इय) कुलोद्भवः 2 माधवाख्य तस्य पुत्रः सोमनस्नेष्ठः । तस्य भार्ग्यां परवपा । तयोज्जीताय महलपस्नेष्ठाय 3 उदकपूर्वं ताम्ब्र(म्र) शासनं कृत्वा प्रदत्तमस्माभिभ्र्माविभिः भ्रूमिपालैर्म्मनुनो [क]धर्म्मा(र्म्म) गौरवात् परिपालनीयमिति ॥ राज(ज्ञ)तः शासनं लब्ध्वा पुनरय'प्रामः' । गृहस्थानमुद्यानस्थानञ्च । स(श)त मुरा धान्योत्वन्यभूमिश्च स्व'श)स्यशेष ईत्या । जलम्बा(म्बो) राख्य 4 प्रामनिवासी । वभ्य(वैइय) सा(शा)ख उपमन्यस्य गोत्रस्य ॥ द्विजोत्तमः । पिहलस(श)र्म्मः । तस्य पुत्रः करंटमनापकः । तस्य भार्ग्यां रैकयोः तयोज्जीतेन । मापयनायकेन सह त्रिस(श)-तेभ्यः ब्राह्मणेभ्यः अप्रहार' कृत्वा उत्तरायण निमित्तो । महलेयस्नेष्ठिन धारापूर्व्वकं । कुद्दाख्य प्राम' प्रदत्त(त)मिति ॥ अस्य प्रामस्य उत्पन्नकरैः राज्ञां(ज्ञां) दि(दे)यः स(श)त मरु धान्योरष्ट-माडैश्च ॥
Manu says:—'पशनां रक्षणं दानमिज्याध्ययनमेव च ।
वणिक पथं कुसीद' च वैश्यस्य कृषिरेव च ॥'
हारीत writes:— 'गोरक्षां कृषि वाणिज्ये कुर्याक्वैश्यो यथाविधि'
पराशर writes:— 'लाभकर्म तथा रत्नं गवां च परिपालनम् ।
कृषि कम' च वाणिज्य' वैश्यवृत्तिरुदाहता' ॥
'बीजानामुप्तिविच्च स्यात् क्षेत्रबीजगुणस्य च
मानयोगांश्च जानीयात्तुलयोगांश्च सर्व'शः ।
सारासारं च भांझनां देशानां च गुणागुणम्
लाभालाभ' च पण्यानां पशनां च विवर्द्धनम् ।
राज्ञे दत्वा तु षड्भागं देवानां चैव विंशकम्।
त्रिंशभागं ब्रह्मणानां कृषिं कूर्बन् न दोषभाक्।॥
(पराशरस्मृति-माधवीयटीका समेत' Telugu Edition of 1875, p. 98.)
cells.notes:
2. According to Dharmasastras , the professions of the वैश्य are cultivation, cowherdship and trade ('कृषि गोरक्षवाणिज्य' वैश्यकम' स्वभावजन्म । गीता ।)
3. Probably he is the father of Bhima Nayaka whose son Gokarna nayaka is the donee of the grant of Vajrahastadeva of ९ 99r
4. It is identified with Jelmur_village in the Srikakulam District.

Ll. 26-57: कलिङ्गनगरात् परममाहेश्वर परमभट्टारक महाराजाधिराज विकलिङ्गाधिपति श्री मदनन्तवर्मा वज्रहस्तदेव: कुशली [||] समस्तामात्य प्रमुख जनपदान ममाहय समाज्ञापयति विदितमस्तु भवतां ॥ कोल्लुयत्तिनी विषये आवरेङ्गाख्य ग्रामः । चनःसीमावच्छिन्नतः सजलस्थलः सर्वपीडा विवर्जित माचन्टाकर्कचितिसमकालं यावन्मातापिचोरात्मनः पग्य-यशोभिवृद्धये ॥ करवसुनिभिणाव्यावृते । उत्तरायणमं क्रान्ग्यौ 1 अम्मिन गामनिवासिने । जलेश्वरदेवाय भोगकृतं ॥ विश्वा[मित्र] गोत्रोत्पन्नः एग्य(प'म. । अस्ग पत्रः । माघयः अस्य भार्य्या कश्चपा । तयोर्जातायं एरयमाय मादर मनवर्त्तिकं प्रदत्तं ॥ अस्यैव ग्रामस्य सीमानो लिख्यन्ते । पूर्व्यतः निव सहित बल्मीकः । परतः वनराजी आग्नेयतः तिन्त्रिणीकवृक्षः त्रिकूटः दक्षिणतः वनराजी । परतः सा वनराजी त्रिकूटः । तैञ्छत्यतः गर्त्तां त्रिकूटः । पश्चिमतः अर्जुनाख्य गर्त्तां । परतः तिन्त्रिणीकवृक्ष सहित सेतुः । वायव्यतः मण्डलाकारपापाणाः सहित गर्त्तां । द्रौ गर्त्तौ सङ्गमेव । परतः अर्जुन वृक्षः । तत्परतः तिन्त्रिणीक वृक्षौ द्रौ । ऐशान्यतः निम्व सहित वाल्मीकः । परतः गर्त्तां समीप त्रिकूटः । अनेन महाक्षशालये वालेयोजाया स्वर्णलौहकारी च मनवर्त्तिका-स्मिन् ग्रामे प्रदत्ता ।
महाकायस्थ(स्त) मन्धिविग्रहि माधुग्ग्य सूनुता दामोदरेण लिखितं । महाचाक्षशालि नु'कमोजुस्य सूनुता बल्लेमोजेन* उत्कीर्णितं ॥

cells.king: Vajrahastadeva § 984 (?) [Sept. N. I. type; Lng. Sans.] Ed:- by Dr. Konow in Ep. Ind. vol. 1X, p. 96
cells.date: शक 984
cells.object: Madras Museum plates of Vajrahastadeva § 984 (?) [Sept. N. I. type; Lng. Sans.] Ed:- by Dr. Konow in Ep. Ind. vol. 1X, p. 96
cells.remarks: The find spot of the plates is not known. They are kept in the Government Museum, Madras. The plates are five in number. attached to a ring which contains the royal seal with the emblems of a bull, a conch, two umbrellas (or lag-staffs), a lamp-stand and a daggar. [After the Prasasti as shown in Appx 1-A upto the end of the verse 12]:— 2. The grant is made on the occasion for a solar-eclipse. Dr. Konow reads the date as शक 984, because, for the word कृत he means युग or the number 4. But, in शक 984 there is no solar eclipse visible in India. So, the date is doubtful. If, however, कृत is taken as a mistake by the scribe for ऋत, then the date will be शक 986 when there are two solar eclipses occurred in वैशाख and कात्तिक, corresponding respectively to the 9th Apl. and 12th oct. of 1064 A. D. But, Bhandarkar suggests to read it as शक 983, and for the corresponding date he hits upon the 20th June, 106I A. D. (Vide E. I. XX Appx. p. 147, No. 1095)

L. 40-54:- कलिगनगरा ता(त्प)रममाहेश्वर परमभट्टारक महाराजाधिराज त्रिकलिङ्गाधि-पति श्रीमदनन्वम्पर्व बज्रहस्तदेवः कुशली [॥] समस्तामात्प्रमुखजनपदान् समाहूय समाज्ञापयति विदितमस्त् भवतां । वराहवन्नैन्यां । तामरन्नेरु ग्रामो 1 नाम चिखलिवाटिकेन सममेकीकृत्य ॥ चतुस्सीमावच्छिन्नस्सजलस्थल सर्व्वपीडाविवर्जितमाचन्द्रावकं क्षितिसम-कालं यावनमातापित्रोरात्मनः पुण्ययशोभिवृद्धये कृतवसुनिधि शाकाव्दे । सूर्य्यग्रहोपरागे 2 विदृढभ्यो यजनयाजनाध्ययनाध्यापन दान प्रतिप्रहृष्टकर्मनिरते भ्यो वृह्ववक्षिचौ [मभ्यः 3॥ पञ्च-शत ब्राह्मणेभ्यः उदकपर्वकं कृत्याग्रहारोस्माभिः प्रदत्तस्तस्माद्भाविभिर्भूमिपालैर्मम् नुनो [क्रत] धर्म्मगौरवा त्परिपालनीयमिति ॥ अपरं च । कोटीश्वर देवाय आचन्द्राक्कं पर्यन्तं निर्वि-रोधा । वलिचरु नैवेद्य दीपपूजाद्यर्थं धान्यमुरक 4 शतद्रयोत्पत्यो(त्या) भूमिर्हत्तां । अत्र च । खण्डस्फाटित भग्नघटनं तत्रस्थ बाह्यणेरकस्य कर्त्तव्यमिति [॥]

Rangacharya in his work in Vol. I, p. 707, No. 399 remarks that the date of this inscription is शक 990, and Vajrahasta is the grandfather of Ananta-varma (Chodaganga). The word विरिचि or ब्रह्मा stands also for the number one, according to the following verse quoted from an unpublished book (preserved in the Orissa State Museum, manuscript Library) named कविकंठहार by Lokanatha Tripathi (an ancestor of the author, S. N. Rajaguru):— (Vidé the कविक'ठहार Ch. 2) If, therefore, the date of the record will be शक 910 (A. D. 988), then the king should be identified with Vajrahastadeva IV (979-1014 A. D.) insread of Vajrahastadeva V (1039-70 A. D.) Any way, the word अव्जसम्भव (ब्रह्मा) according to the Dirghasi inscription of the time of Rajarajadeva (No. 15), denotes the number 9. So, the date of this inscription is probably शक 990 of the time of Vajrahasta V

cells.remarks: * This inscription is on a slab to the right of the main entrance of मधुकेश्वर temple at Mukhalinga. 1. If Vajrahasta V. is the same king whose name is mentioned in it, then his 39th regnal year will correspond to 1077 A. D., since he ascended the throne in एक ९60 (A.D. 1038). But his reign ended, according to many other inscriptions, in 1069 A.D. Therefore, I presume that either the regnal year, as given in it, is incorrect or the king is Vajrahasta III who ruled for 44 years. I think the R. Y. given in this record is not correct. 4. The language, used in this incsription, seems to be Oriya. It is one of the few inscriptions where Oriya-Prakrit had been adopted during that period. In the preface to the V volume of the South Indian Inscriptions in 1925 H.Krishna Sastri, the Government Epigraphist for India, had admitted that the texts of the Oriya inscriptions were tentative for want of published inscriptions in that language and script and also scholars capable of handling them were few

cells.notes:
1. The corresponding date is the 15th June, 1069 A. D. The 7th tithi must have ended on the previous day i. e. the 14th June, 1069 A. D. if it was of the पूर्णिमान्त system; otherwise it wolud be the 29th June, 1069 A. D. if it is of the अमान्त system. Here also the 7th tithi ended on the previous day, i. e. on the 28th June, 1069 A. D.
2. The correct reading is probably वैशव'शोद्धव. The word वेश्या indicating the dancing girl, is not to be totaly rejected as the Vesya caste was also supported by the Ganga kings of Kalinga.

cells.text_original: अनन्वर्म चोडगङ्गदेयः कुशली [!] समस्तामात्र प्रमुखजनपदान् समाहूय समाज्ञापयति विदितमस्तु भवतां ॥ वराहवर्तन्यां ऋष्टनग्रामश्चतुस्सीमावच्छिन्नसजलस्थलस्सर्वपीडाविवर्जितमाचन्द्राकर्षितिसमकालं यावन्मातापित्रोरात्मनश्च पुण्ययशोभिवृद्धये ॥ हरनयनवियद्गगन चन्द्रगणिते शाकाब्दे मीनमाम् कृष्णपञ्चम्यामादियवारे1 सामान्यतो नानागोत्रेभ्यः यजनयाजनाध्ययनध्यापनदानपतिपद्वषट्कर्मनिरते भ्यः चिशतवाहरोभ्यः धारापूर्वकमस्माभिदत्त इत्यम्य ग्रामम्य सीमालिङ्गानि लिखयन्ते ॥ पूर्व्वर्तः खोन्न होम्वरवेलिल तोनेङ्गि ग्रामानां तृ(त्रि)कट नोनेङ्गि ग्राम वक्र गर्त्तां । आग्नेयनः वल्मीक सहित मरीच वृक्षः । तत्पश्चिमतः वक्रगत्वा मरीचवृक्ष पंक्तिः । ततः खोन्ननोनेङ्गि खोल्लेर ग्रामाणां तृ(त्रि)कूटे वाल्मीक सद्वित मरीचवृक्षः । दक्षिणम्यां दिग्गि वृहद्वाल्मीकः । तत् पश्चिमतः वनराजिका । नैऋत्यां खोन्नकोल्लेर तूलुबु ग्रामाणां तृ(त्रि)कूटे तनुवापिका गर्त्तां च । पश्चिमायां गर्त्तां । वायव्यतः खोन्नन्तुलुबु गार ग्रामाणां गर्त्तां तीर तृ(त्रि)कूटः ॥ खोन्नगार होम्वरवेलिल ग्रामां तोनेङ्गि गर्त्तां तृ(त्रि)कूटः ॥ [After this there follow two ग्रोकाs from Dharmma Śstra] मदाक्षा(का)यस्थ स्त) सन्धिविग्रहि मावुत्य सूनुना दामोदरेण लिखित' । मदाक्षगान्धी वल्ले गेजेनोत्कीर्णे तः (इति)॥

cells.remarks: Rangacharya's Vol. I, p.707; no. 95, Noticed in Bhandarkar's list No. 1955; J.A.S.B. Vol. LXXII, pt. i, p 102, Nos. 3 & 4. *: On a slab to the left of the 2nd entrance into the temple of Madhukesvara I. In S. I. I. it is read as '100(o) 6', although no symbol for '6' is there. The Government Epigraphist reads the date as 100[5] in A. R. no. 244 of 1896. Rangacharya, as usual, has copied it and says that Anantavarmadeva ruled from 1075-1146 A. D. So, the 8th श्राहि corresponds to ३. 1005 or 1083 A. D. But, from the copperplate grant of अनन्तवम चोडगङ्गदेव it is found that his accession took place in S. 999 or 1077 A. D. (for details see Appendix II-A). Accordingly, his 8th श्राहि is equal to S. 1003-04. Since this record and no. 24 are issued for the occasion of उत्तरायण स'क्रांति in the same regnal year of चोडगङ्ग, the शक year in both the cases ought to be the same. It may further be noted here that if the श्राहि of चोडगङ्गदेव was started from the day of 'Suniya' or the 12th tithi of the bright fortnight of भाद्रपद, then the 8th श्राहि will start from the 6th August, 1082 A. D. and end on the 27th August, 1082 A. D. Accordingly, the उत्तरायण स'क्रांति of S. 1004 or 1082 A. D. will fall in his 8th regnal year

चोडगङ्गदेवः कुशली । समस्तामात्य प्रमुख जनपदात् समाहूय समाज्ञापयति विदितमस्तु भवतां एरडविषये मुरुपाक ग्रामश्चतुम्सौमावच्छिन्न स्मज्जलस्थल सर्वपीड्वा विवर्जितमाचन्द्राकर्षे चिति समकाल यावन्मातापित्रोरात्मवज्र प्राययशोभिवृद्धये ॥ भूतगगनविर्यत ] शशि गणिते शकाव्दे उत्तरायण सक्कान्त्यां* नरेन्द्रेश्च(श्वरदेवस्य पूजा निवेदय जुल्पमीतवादूय करणाय विमानस्य खण्डपुत्रेत[त]संस्काराय! चास्माभिर्दत्त इति ॥ अस्मिनग्रामे भारद्वाज गोढस्य दारपञ्चम्म(म्मै)णः पुत्तः चामेनशम्मर्य तच्(च्छ्रा)स्स(य)च्छ्राच्छ्राद्र(त्र) दामोदगस्य पुत्रो रेमनाख्य(ख्यः) अस्य कुल समद्भूत प्रोलयशु(स)त नावनाख्य(ख्यः) पिन्नपि शु सुत अयितनाख्य(ख्यः) वालेरु श(म)त गोपनाख्यः । एने पञ्च गधा(इया)ध्मं परिकल्पित वृत्त्यां देवस्थानस्य रक्षा स्थापिता इति ॥ अस्य प्राप्तम्य मीमालिङ्गानि लिखयन्ते । पूर्व्यतः स्थापित शिला । तद्दक्षिणतः मुरुपाक नपिटयाटन वर शीमाणां तृ(त्रि)कूटे गुमुरु 2 वासिका । आग्ने-यतः मुरुपाक लोवनवर ग्राम मा)णां तृ(त्रि)कूटे स्थापित शिला । ततो वायव्यतः स्थापितशिला तत्पश्चिमतः तित्रिणी समूह । तद्दक्षिणतः स्थापितशिला । तत्पश्चिमतः तित्रिणी समूह । तद्दक्षिणतः वल्मीकः[।] तत्पर्वतः वल्मीकः । तदाग्नेयतः वल्मीकः । तद्दक्षिणतः मुरुपाक लेखरह श्रीमस्तरु ग्रामाणां त्रिकूटे स्थापित शिला । तद्दक्षिणतः ककवनराजि । दक्षिणस्यांदिशि उष-

रस्थ वल्मीकः । तदुत्तरतः तिंत्रिणीसमूह । तत्पश्चिमतः तिंत्रिणी समूह ! तद्दक्षिणतः निव्वण वृक्षः । तत्पश्चिमतः तटाकसेतौ स्थापित शिला · तद्दक्षिणतः मुरुपाक लोब क्रोश्वेर ग्रामाणां त्रिकूटे तटाकसेतौ तिंबिणी वृक्षः । नैऋट्यां दिशि मुरुपाक क्रोश्वेर त्रिजयपुर ग्रामाणां तृ(त्रि)-कूटे गर्त्त [1] पश्चिमायांदिशि मुरुपाक भिजयपुर बुरुमुर ग्रामाणां दृ(त्रि)ड्रूटे गर्त्त । बायव्यादिशि मुरुपाक बुरुमूर वीमाद ग्रामाणां दृ(त्रि)कूटस्थ गुल्मः । तत्पूर्वतः गोमूत्र वक्रेण वल्मीकः[1] ततः ईषद् वक्रेण पूर्वतो वल्मीकः[1] तदुत्तरतः तिंत्रिणी वृक्षः [1] तत्पूर्वतः वल्मीकः । तदुत्तरतः मुरुपाक वोमद रेङ्ग ग्रामाणां दृ(बि)कूटे पर्वतिका [1] उत्तरस्थां दिशि भूशिलाः[1] तदाग्नेयतः पव्वंतिका शिखरं । तदाग्नेयतः वल्मीकः [1] तत् पूर्वतः तिंत्रिणी पर्वित(ङ्किंत) [1] ईशान्यां दिशि तिंत्रिणी वृक्षः ॥ बहुभिर्व्वंसुधा दत्ता राजभिस्सगरादिभिः । यस्य यस्य यदा भूमिस्तस्थ तस्य तदा फलम् । स्वदत्तां परदत्ताम्बा यो हरेत वसुन्धरां स विष्ठायां क्रमिर्भूत्वा पितृमिस्सह पच्यते । मा(म)हाकायस्थ सन्धिविग्रहि माबुराय सूनुना दामोदरेण लिखितम् । मा(म)हाक्षशालि बल्लेमोजेनांत्कर्णर्न(र्णम्) ॥

cells.remarks: I. 'पूजारे' or the 'Archakas' of the temple of मधुकेश्वर at Mukhalingam(Srikakulam Dt.) are the Kalingis Among the Kalingis there are two important sections namely: किन्ताल कालिंगि and वूरगां-कालिंगि. The letter sub caste use the sacred thred like ब्राह्मण. The' titles used by them are नाइडु, नायलु', चौधुरी, विशोषी, पधान, जेन्ना, खाइं and नायिक ( Vide castes and Tribes of southern India , by Tharston, Vol. III p. 49), Their mother tongue is some times Oriya and some times Telugu. Except the first two titles as given above, the rest of the titles are also used by the Khandaits in Orissa. At present they are not using the caste title of 'भरट', as in the case of मधव भर्र in the present inscription. The Kalingis are the ancient inhabitants of Kalinga. Their caste-people are not living beyond the south of Anakapalli in Visakhapatnam District. In Ganjam they are known as Kalinji and they use the caste titles of वराट, वारिक, बेहरा, दलाइ, गउड, मलिक, पात्र, पुलाइ, राउत, सान्त, साहु, गुरु etc. (See Thurston's castes and Tribes of Southern India, Vol. III p. 50)

cells.remarks: Rangacharya's Vol. I, Ganjam, no. 88, † This inscription is on a slab right of the entrance into the आस्थान म'ष्प of the temple of Madhukesvara. I. श्री जयनाथ was a ब्राह्मण सण्डलिक पोत. He seems to be the commander-in-chief like Vanapati under the kings राजराज and his son चोडग'न. He defeated many enemy-kings in favour of his master, चोडग'न. His father was a मांडलिक named गन्धवारण ब्रह्म चक्रवर्ति. The title 'श्रीभारती' seems to have been used by श्रीनाथ as a family title. Generally speaking this title was used by the 'Avadhutas', according to the following verses of ब्रह्म राक्कर विजयम्, quoted in a book named 'अवधूताश्रम'- अवधूता दशाथ। यथा ब्रह्मच्छक्कर विजये- (Vide Notices of Sanskrit MSS . Second series, by Mm. H. Sastri, Vol. III, pt. i, p. 8). But, the title 'श्रीभारती' is used here as a family designation

cells.remarks: © This inscription is found on the 1st and 2nd faces of the slab at Ronanki which also contains the inscription No. 38 above, 1 The epithet नवनवतिसहत्त्रकुजराधीश्वर indicates that चोडगग्गे was the lord of 99,000 elephants. Probably his war potentiality was immence, According to the old system of forming battalion for the armies in India, as described in No. 141 (f. n. 3), a गुल्म will consist of 9 chariots + 9 elephants + 27 horses + 45 feet-soldiers Hence, if चोडगग्गे had 99,000 elephants, then he might have proportionately maintained 11,000 गुल्म (battalions), which consisted of 99,000 chariots + 99,000 elephants + 1,97,000 horses + 4.95,000 foot-soldiers. There is tittle doubt, however, that a huge army was in his possession while his empire was extended from the Godavari in the South and the Ganges in the north, including some fewdatory states in the western parts of his Kingdom

Actually, the 8th tithi falls on the previous day, i. e. Saturday. It should be noted here that there is a long gap in time be between Nos. 40 and 41. Probably there appeared some troubles during this period in Kalinga, for which reason the normal activities in social life were suspended. I think, the Cholas, who invaded Kalinga at different times as is evident from the descriptions given in Kalingattu Parani (Vide App IV) and in an inscription of the Bhimesvara temple at Draksharam (Vide S.I.I. Vol IV no. 1239) are responsible for prevalence of an abnormal condition there

Bhogapur still goes under the same name. It is an ancient place of Kalinga. According to a copperplate inscription of Kokilivarman of the E. Chalukya family (A. R. 1909, p. 106), Bhogipura was a Vishaya (district) of Madhyama-Kalinga. From another stone inscription of 1109, found in Bhogapuram (Vide A. R. no. 363 of 1905), we learn that in the time of the Ganga king Anantavarman (राज राज देव II), the third son of चोडग'ग देव, a merchant named कण्णम नायक constructed a Jaina temple called राजराज जिनालय, in the same place. Most probably that name was selected after the name of the Ganga king Anantavarma Rajaraja II who ruled from 1170-71 A. D. to 1190 A. D. (Vide O.H.R J. Vol. V, Nos. 1 & 2, the Kenduli plates of Narasimhadeva IV, App. "II)

D. and 1088-9 to atleast 1092-3 A. D. ( E. I. VI, p. 335). He married a Ganga princess ( S.I.I. III no. 120)

cells.object: Gudivadā village (Visakhapatna Dt.) S. (?) Rangacharya's vol. III, Vizagapatam no. II
cells.remarks: The text of this inscription is not available. Rangacharya says that it is a damaged stone inscription, lyng in the village of Gudivadā in Visakhapatna District. As no text is available and I had no opportunity to examine the original of it, there is no other option left except quoting the note given by Rangacharya as follows:— “On a stone in the middle of the street, An undated private grant in the reign of Śrī Anantavarmadeva (1077-1146)” As the date of the record is not associated with it, we can hardly identify the king Anantavarman with Chodagangadeva, because Anantavarman is used as a title by all Ganga kings after Vajrahasta V

cells.king: Anantavarmadeva
cells.object: Gudivada village (Vishakhapatam) § (?) Rangacharya's Vol. III. p. 166, Vizagupitam, No. 12
cells.remarks: The text of this inscription is also not available like No. 45 above. It is also found in the same village of Gudivada of Visakhapatna district. Rangacharya's brief note is, therefore, quoted below:— “In the same place (where No. 45 is found). Grant by a Gokarparajat of Gudivada in the reign of Anantavarmadeva.” † It is interesting to note here that the name Gokarna tempts one to identify him with the famous गोकण्ठ who is said to have defeated along with his master चोङ्गण देव by Ratnadeva II (r120-33 A. D.) of the Chedi family of तुमाण. In the Pendrabandha copper plate inscription of Pratapamalla we get the following versi:- (Vide E. I. XXIII, p. 4 ). If गोकण्ठ of the Cheddi record is identical with गोकण्ठ राज of Gudivada, then the king Anantavarman might be the same as चोङ्गण गदेव. Another गोकण्ठ is mentioned in Dirghasi inscription of the time of Rajaraja I (1070-78 A. D.) (Vide No. 12). According to that inscription, he was the father of Vanapati, a शह्मण of आत्रेय रोत्र and a commander of Rajaraja I. 1NSCRIPTIONS OF ORISSA

cells.remarks: Rangacharya's Vol. I, p. 701, Ganjam, no. 309. * It is on the 1st pillar at the right row of the आस्थानम'डप, south face, of the temple of Madhukesvara. It is necessary to note here that the last known inscription before this record is dated 24-12-1108 A. D. So, there is a gap of about two years between the Nos. 48 and 49. It is an unusual silence period during the long reign of Chodaganga. Why such thing had happened? What caused the social and religious activities suspend in his kingdom? I presume that that was the period when चोडगग्ग had conquered Utkala and Vengi, and subjugated both the kingdoms, according to the following verse which was added to his Prasasti in the copperplate inscriptions incised on or after 1112 A. D

He seems to have taken active parts in several battles to help his brother. As his mother राजसुन्दरी was the daughter of Rajendra chola, the selection of the name पेमांडि has got influence of Tamil, according to which 'Perumall' is the name of a Vaishnavite deity. In some inscriptions परमदि'देव used the surname of उलगुखवन्द which surname was also used by the Chola king Kulottunga III (Vide A. R. no. r25 of 1912),

It corresponds to the 18th October, 1111 A.D. The Government Epigraphist in A. R. no 210 of 1896 reads the date as S. I 032 which was also copied by Ranga-charya. The word "Nayana" here is referred to 'Haranayana' which stands for three. Because, in शक 1033 in the month of तुल we get the lunar eclipse which is referred to in this inscription. We get the following passage relating to three in कविक'ठशर by Lokanatha Tripathi. Here the word 'ईशनेत्र' is given, but not 'नेत्र'. In the Indian Palaeography , G H. Ojha writes at page I20 that the following words indicate the number two:-लोचन, नेत्र, अक्षि, चक्षु, नयन etc. In No. 55 'हरनयन' for three is mentioned. But, here it is नयन

cells.date: 1114 A. D
cells.object: Lingaraja temple of Bhubaneswar † S. 1084 [Sept: N. I. Type; Lng. Snsk.] Ed.—by Dr. K. C. Panigrahi in O.H.&J. Vol. I, no. ii, p. 7,
cells.remarks: † The inscription is on the inner wall of the Jagamohana of the temple of लिङ्गराज. I Dr. D. C. Sircar suggests to read ब्रह्मरामखे'दु गणिते or शक 1036 (1114 A. D). But, Chodaganga's 37th श्राद्धि is ended on the 5th September, 1112 A. D. (Vide App. II-C). So, Dr. Panigrahi's reading seems to be correct. Chodaganga's name, for the first time, is given in this inscription. So, Dr. Panigrahi suggests that his (Chodaganga's) conquest of Utkala must have taken place in or before 1112 A. D. I fully agree with this view and add in note r to no. 40 above that since no inscription bearing the name of Chodaganga is found in Kalinga between 11108-1111 A. D. there is the possibility that within this period he engaged himself in wars against Vengi and Utkala

cells.remarks: The plates have been discovered from Korni, a village in Srikakulam district. They are five in number, attached to a ring containing the usual Ganga seal with the emblems of a bull, a conchshel, a chauri etc. [After the Prasasti as shown in App. I-C including the additions in the foot-note] L!. 106-136 1 The corresponding date is either the 20th March (the 4th tithi ) or the 20th Feb. (the last day of कुम्भ), IoS2 A. D., Sunday (= हरनयतवे स्दानवन्द्र= Io03 शक, मोन कृष्ण पचमो आदित्यवार). It seems Vajrahasta, the grandfather of Chodaganga had formerly granted the village in favour of Brahmanas. Then, again Chodaganga granted the same in शक Io34 (वेदगुणवियच्चन्द्र). For a similar obliteration of original grant see E. I. XXIII. p. 101 n

श्रीचोडगङ्गदेवः वराद्वर्तिनीविषये(ग)[नि]वासिनो राष्ट्रकूटप्रमुखान् कुद्मिवन स्सर्वान् स्समाहय गुरोद्विनामात्ययुवगजमभिविग्रांहि दौवाञ्छिक् प्रमुख परंजन समज्जमित्थमाज्जापयति विदितमस्तु वो यथा । भवद्विषये खोन्नग्रामः मुडपरु नाम ग्रामं ग्रासीकृत्वा चतुस्सीमावच्छिन्ननस्सजलस्थल स्सर्वपीडाविवर्जितमाचन्द्राक्कर्षे नितिसमकालं यन्मातापित्रोरात्मनश्च पुन्यं(ण्य) यशोभिवृद्धये हरनयतवियद्गुरागनचन्द्रगणिते पु शकवत्सरेपु मौनमास कृष्णपचम्यामादित्यवारे। सामान्यतो नानागोत्रेभ्योऽध्ययनाध्यापन यजनयाजनदान-प्रतिग्रहषट्कम्मं निरतं भ्यञ्चिराद् व ह्वाणेभ्यो धारापूर्वकं मत्प्रि(पि)तामहेन घञ्जहस्नदेवेन दत्तं । तत्र गार ग्राम गुरीत मुडपरु ग्रामस्य प्रतिक्षेत्रत्वेन तूलुवृग्रामादादृन्याग्रोत्तराशीति परिमितं क्षेत्रं तेभ्यः खोन्नग्राम निशासि वाग्रणेभ्यः वेदगुणवियच्चन्द्रगणिते पु शकवत्सरे-षूत्तरायण निमित्तं 2 धारापूर्वकमस्माभिर्दत्तमिति । अस्य क्षेत्रस्य प्रतिक्षेत्रेण सार्द्धं
'पीमालिङ्गानि पूर्व्यतः खोन्न ओम्वरवेल्लि तानेङ्कि ग्रामानां तृ(त्रि)कूटे तोनेंगग्राम यक्रगत्तौ[]] आग्नेयतः वाल्मीक सहित मरीच वृक्षः। तत् पश्चिमतः ईषद्वक्र'गत्वा वृक्षप'क्तिः[]] ततः खोन्नतोनेंगि खोल्लिरग्रमानां त्रिकूटे वाल्मिक सहित मरीचवृक्षः। दक्षिणस्यां दिशि बृहद्-वाल्मीकः। तत् पश्चिमतः वनराजिका'[]] ततोगत्तौ उल्ल'ध्य स्थापित शिला। ततः क्रमेण स्थापित' शिलात्रय'। नैऋत्यां दिशि स्थापित शिला। ततः ई (?)णि दलसेतोरधस्तिन्त्रणी-वृक्ष समीपे स्थापित शिला ततस्तटाक प्रविष्ट' गत्तं मुख'। ततो गत्तौतीरे स्थापितशिला। ततो गत्तैव। वायव्य दिशायां गत्तीय सन्धौ तिन्त्रिणी वृक्ष समीपे स्थापित शीला। ततो गत्तां-तुसारेणो प्राचीदिश' किञ्चिद्वक्र'गत्वा तो गत्तांमुल्ल'ध्य गत्वा खोन्नतुलुबु गारग्रामाणां त्रिकूटे गत्तं द्वय मध्ये स्थापित शिला। उत्तरस्यां दि'श तटाकद्वय सेतु स धिः। ईशान्दिशायां खोन्नगार ओम्वरवेल्लि ग्रामानां तोनेंगगत्तौतीरत्रिकः। अस्योपरि नकेनचिद्वाधः तथाहि व्यासेन भगवतोक्त'। बहुभिर्व्वसुधा दत्ता राजभिस्सगरादिभिर्य्यस्य यध्य यदा भूमिस्तस्य तस्य नदा फलम्[]]। स्वदत्तां परदत्ताम्बा यत्नाद्रक्ष युधिष्ठिर[]]महीम्महीमतां श्रेष्ठ दानाच्छे-योनुपालनम्[]]। गामेक' स्वर्णमेक' वा भूमेरप्येकमंगुलं हरन्नरक माप्नोति यावदाभूतसंप्लवम्[]]। स्वदत्तां परदत्तां वा यो हरेत वसुन्धरां षष्ठि वर्षसहस्राणि विष्ठायां जायते कृमिः[]]इति कर्त्ताकाव्यस्य शासनाधिकारी नावदि भट्टः। लेखको षल्लेनाचार्य्य मुतो वट्टताचार्य्यः।
cells.notes: 2 The corresponding date is the 24th Dec. 1112 A. D.

cells.object: Lingaraja temple (Bhubaneswar)* [Sept. N. I. Type; Lng. Snsk.] Deciphered by me from the original
cells.remarks: * The beginning of each line is broken. I श्रीवीरचोइ cannot be teken for श्री वीरचोड[गगदेव]. Because, the full name of the king in all the votive inscriptions are given as श्रीमन्श्रनतवमं देव. Here, the name वीरचोड is quite clear. He, according to my opinion, is the son of Kulottunga-Rajendrachoda and most probably the father-in-law of चोडगगदेव. He seems to have assisted his son-in-law at the moment when strategical actions were necessary. (see my notes in O.B.R.J. vol. V pp. 5-2-55). वीरचोड was the Viccray of Vengi upto 1092-3 A. D. Afterwords he seems to have settled in Kalinga (see also notes 3 at No. 44 above)

cells.remarks: † This is the first known earliest inscription relating to a donor of Orissa and Kalinga found at Simhachalam temple on the 8th niche of the outer verandah 2. Read वाराण्यी कटक. The capital of the Ganga kings of Orissa, who, after shifting their administration from Kalinga-nagara, located it at अभिनव वाराण्यी कटक which has been identified with the modern city of Cuttack. The earliest known stone inscription where अभिनव वाराण्यी कटक is mentioned belongs to शक 1300 (1378 A. D.). It is found in the temple of Simhachalam ( S. I. I. Vol. VI, No. 851). B. it, in शक 1151 महाराजा अनियक्कुर्भेम III granted his Nagari plates from this town ( B. I. XXVIII, p. 235). His queen's Kanchipuram inscription also mentions the name of that town

cells.remarks: Rangacharya's Vol. I, p. 703, Ganjam, no. 335. † It is on the 3rd pillar in the right row of the आस्थान म'डप, north face in the temple of Madhukesvara. I The significant feature of this grant is that in commemoration of the "पितृतिथि" or the death-ceremony of the father of the donor, it is arranged to burn a perpetual lamp before Madhukesvara during दामोदरपूजा in the month of कार्तिक. This पूजा is mainly performed by widows in Orissa (for कार्त्तिकदामोदर see App. V.) According to the "हयशीपेप'चरात्र" the image of Damodara will be as follows: Four arms. In the upper left arm there is शह्न (conch) and in the lower left arm there is चक्क (disk). Similarly, the upper and lower arms of the right there are पद्म and गदा. This is a prototype of the image named Aniruddha of the Chaturvyuha images. A kind of शालग्राम is also known as दामोदर. It is described as follows:—

In the copperplate inscriptions of the early Ganga Kings of Kalinga, their long Prasasti begins with the phrase of “महेन्द्राचलामलकनकशिखरप्रतिष्ठितस्य सचराचरगुरोस्सकल-भुवननिर्माणैकसूक्ष्मारस्य शशाक्करोखरस्य श्रीयोक्ण्येश्रभट्यरकस्य ” etc. This God Gokarnesvara is, therefore, installed on the Mahendra mountain since the 7th century A, D, and he was the family deity of the Gangas for more than four-hundred years until the Gangas shifted their headquarters from Kalinganagara and were converted into Vaishnavism

The occasion for the grant is कन्यमास ऋष्णाष्टमी which corresponds to the 8th tithi of the dark fortnight of the month of आश्विन. According to the religious customs observed in Orissa, it happens to be the day when the sixteen-days Puja (शरत्कालीन दुर्गोत्सव) relating to the goddess Durga is performed. The day is, therefore, quite auspicious for grants. The सहस्रक्रमविधि is also observed on this sacred day. According to Rangacharya, the beginning of the inscription is built in. But, it is not so. Because, the record is complete. The Government Epigraphist has not given the श्राद्धि year of this record but he gives राक 1045 which is not there. So, the A. R. no. of this record is not correctly put in S. I. I. Vol.V, no. 1037. 3. The term नकरपुवाडनायक seems to be either a title of the headman of नकरपुवाड or कलिङ्गनगर or a synonym of नगरश्रेष्टि. The title नगरश्रेष्टि is found in Damodarpur plates of the Gupta period (Vide E. I. XV. ). In this connection R. G. Basak says that a स्त्रियवपति who is the head of a विश्व was aided by four advisors. One of the advisors was called नगरश्रेष्टिन्. He had to represent the various guilds or corporations of the town or the rich urban population. The remaining three advisors were known as प्रथमसाथवाह (the representative of merchant class), प्रथमकुलिक (the representative of the artisan class) and प्रथमकायस्थ (probably the chief scribe, the head of the Government Officials). Dr. U. N. Ghoshal in his Hindu Revenue System writes that the district officers were “carring on the administration of the district-town (अधिधानाधिकरण) with a guild-president, the leading merchant, the leading banker and the leading scribe at the top”. (Vide History of North-Eastern India , p. 202). The guild president (प्रेष्टिच्) and the scribe (कायस्थ), according to the Sanskrit drama मृच्छकटिक, used to assist the अधिकरण in deciding cases. In Rajputana the Chauthias are said to be the town Magistrates. According to William Crooke, “in every town there is an unpaid magistracy, of which the head is the नगरश्च or the chief citizen, and the four chauthias , tantamount to the Loid Mayor and Aldermen, who hold their courts and decide in all civil cases”. (Vide Annuals and Antiquities of Rajasthan , Vol. I. p. 171). For more details regarding नगरश्चेष्ठिन् please see The Journal of The University of Gauhati , Vol. VI. (1955), pp. 81—85

cells.remarks: Rangacharya's Vol. II, p. 733, Godavari Dt., no. 217. † In S. I. I , the number is wrongly put as A. R. 315. 1. The donor is Jayamonda Choda Mahâdevi who is designated as कलिङ्गमहादेवी and पट्ट महादेवी. She is the chief queen of Anantavarma Chodaganga. For the sake of her name, it is presumed that she comes from the Chola family to which her mother-in-law (R)jasundari) belongs. I have discussed about Virachoda and his relation with Chodaganga in O.H.R.J. Vol V, pp. 50-54 and arrived at the conclusion that the Chief-qeen of Chodaganga was the daughter of Virachoda. In South-India the marriage with maternal-uncle's daughter is popular, according to the following verses quoted from धर्मशास्त्र:- No. I05 Draksharama (Godavari Bt)† S 10:0 [Sept. Tel; Lng. Tel.& Snsk.] S. I. I. Vol. IV, no. 1191; A. R. no. 3,6 of 1893; Rangacharya's Vol. II, p. 784, Godavari, no. 221. † In A. R. of 1893 the number is given as 316. But, in S. I. I. , it is put as A. R. No. 312 of 1893. I. The donor is राजलादेवा, a queen of Chodagauga for whom the title of साहसांक is used in this record. It is necessary to state here that there is a Sanskrit work called साहसांकचरित, written by Padmagupta alias Parimala (Vide I.A. 1907). Padmagupta was a court poet of Vakpati Munja of Paramara family (1086 A. D.). As he is a contemporary of Chodaganga, whose title was साहसांक, I think that further research on साहसांक चरित might reveal some new facts in the life history of Chodaganga

cells.remarks: Rangaoharya's Vol. I, p. 682, Ganjam, no. 137. † It is on the a slab lying at the front of the temple. ¹ The number of this inscription is wrongly put as A. R. no. 387 of 1896 in The South Indian Inscriptions . ² The date is corresponding to the 20th April, 1132 A. D. The वैशाख-शुक्ल-तृतीया or अक्षय तृतीया is a fastival day. On this day the wheels of the cars of Jagannatha, Balabhadra and Subhadra are fixed to the axles. This is again the beginning of the day of Treta-Yuga. It is also the birth day of Parasurama alisa Yamadagnya. According to Madhavatirtha, the day of अक्षय-तृतीया is auspecious when it is associated with wednesday and रोहिणी-नक्षत्र. (see Swamikannu Pillai's Indin Ephemeris , Vol I, pt. i p. 60). Our inscription is, therefore, gives an auspecious date which is a Yoga, according to the Vaishnavas. ³ The Srikarana , who is a Vaisya by caste, says that he belonged to the Ganga dynasty. ⁴ The titles of 'padihasta' and 'Purapari' are used by the same person. ⁵ The modern Arsavelli in Srikakulam district is the same village as mentioned in this inscription. It is in Kalinga (vide the temple inscriptions of Draksharama published in S. I. I. Vol. V, no. 1188, line 3)

cells.remarks: † It is on a pillar at the left of the first entrance to the central shrine of the temple of Srikurmam. where upon he pleased the gods, the Rishics, the Pitrs and the Brahmanas by giving charities. After this it is stated that one Medapotu Bhatta, a Brahmana of Harita gotra and Apastambha Sutra who was the Superintendent of the temple (स्थानाधिपति) probably gave some perpetual lamps to burn in the temple. The importance of the temple of Sri Kurmam was increased after Chodaganga accepted the Vaishnuvism, propagated by Ramanuja through विशिष्टाद्वैतवाद. Regarding the stratagical activities of Chodaganga please refer to my paper in O. H. R. J. Vol. V, PP, 59 where I have referred to this inscription. (Author) Vizagapatam plates of Chodagangadev 1 S. 1957- [Sept. Tel; Lng. 'Snsk.] Ed by J. F. Fleet in I. A. Vol. XVIII, P. 172 and noticed by Sewell in Arch, Surv, South-India. Vol II. P. 32. The plates are three in number, attached to a ring containing the seal with the emblems of a bull and acouchant

B., Vol. LXXII, Pt. i, P. 106, no. 31. † It is on the 4th pillar in the right row of the आस्थानम'डप, west face of the temple of Mukhalinga. The officer has used the designation of शासनिक. It is a derivation from शासन which denotes order or command (Vide V, R, Ramachandra Dikshitar's Hindu Administrative Institutions , P. 104) In the copperplate inscriptions of the Gangas of Orissa we get the following verse regarding the Abhisheka of Kāmārṇṇava-deva, son of Choḍagangadeva:- It proves that the ceremony of 'Mūrdhabhisheka' of the नृपवरतनय was taken place at Puri (Jagannātha) in Śuka 1064, in the month of Dhanus, which corresponds to the 24th December, 1142 A. D. In ancient India there was the system of Yuvarajyabhisheka when a prince used to get consecrated during the life time of his father. In the Ramayana it is mentioned that Bharata's two sons were given the charge of the kingdom at Takshaṣilā and Pushkalāvati. Similarly, Śatrṣghna's two sons were posted at Mathura and Vidiśa; Lakhmaṇa's two sons became the governors at the two cities of Kampatha and Rama's two sons held the rulership at Uttara-Kosala and Dakshiṇa-Kosala. (Vide the Ramayana , VII, 101, 11; 108, 9-11; 102,1 and 107, 7). According to Arthasastra (Bk. V, 3), a Yuvaraja is honoured by the king and entitled to get the allowence from the state to the extent of 48,000 'Paṇas' like the Purohita, the Senadhyaksha, the Raja-Māta and the Rṇi. Usually the Yuvaraja held a regular office almost equal in status to a Governor; and he remained as a subordinate to the king. From the epigraphical records of the 7th to 10th centuries A. D. we come across the following titles:- (1) Maharāja (2) Rāja (3) Kumara (4) Amātya (5) Uparika (6) Vishayapati (7) Ayuktaka (8) Chāṭa (9) Bhatṭa etc. The posi- • For details see O. H. R. J. Vol. V , pp 59 - 60. tion of a Kumāra or Yuvarĵja was, in many cases, kept in between the Rāja and Amātya. This order was, however, changed in the time of Choḍagaṅgadeva. In his inscriptions we find the following order: Purohita, Amātya, Yuvarĵja. Sandhivigrahika, Dauvārika etc. So, the Yuvaraja's position was a bit lowered and he was placed between the Amātya and Sandhivigrahika

cells.remarks: † The village Alagum is situated about 23 miles from Puri and 10 miles from Sakhigopal in Puri district. * Here the dandims are not necessary. 1. The grant is made during the 62nd श्राहि of Chodaganga, and in the 7th tithi of the bright fortnight of Magha. According to my calculation as shown in App. II - C, Chodaganga's 62nd श्राहि started from 10 - 8 - 1136 A.D. So, the corresponding date is the 31st December, 1136 A. D. It is necessary to state here that माघ-शुक्ल-सप्तमी is popularly called तिलसप्तमी which is a festival day in Orissa at the banks of the Chandrabhaga river near Konarka in Puri district. Dr. Sircar, while editing this inscription in E. I. , has erred in saying that the 62nd श्राहि will "correspond to 1140 - 41 A. C." In the face of a large number of inscriptions in the reigning period (श्राहि) of the same king, the above view of Dr. Sircar should easily be rejected. It is necessary to give an idea about the coinage in Orissa. From the ancient times the cauri-shell (कपद्दंक ) was used in this country. That was the basic unit of coinage. The following tables are quoted from the लीलावतीसूत्र' and the प्रायश्चिततत्त्वम् of Raghunandana:— According to these tables the total number of कपद्दंक (cauri-shell), equal to 105 पुराण, is 80 × 16 × 105 = 1,34,400

The date portion of this inscription is damaged,except that which gives the श्राहि. In the 2nd line there is a number 8 found after about three mutilated letters. It may be any number of श्राहि. followed by eight. i. e. 18, 28, 38 48, 58 and 68. When we examine the following corresponding Srahi years as per App. II-C with the astronomical combinations as found in the record, it is known that it must be Chodaganga's 64th Srahi:—A.D. 1082, 1094, 1104, 1114, 1122,, 1132, 1142 श्राहि 8, 18, 28, 38, 48. 58. 68. It fits to 1142 and the corresponding da'e is the 5th July 1142 A.D. Sunday. Here again arises a difficulty. The 68th श्राहि started on the 3rd September of that year, according to my assumption, namely that the श्राहि year starts from भाद्रपद शुक्ल द्वादशी. the day of सुनिश्चा in Orissa. This question, therefore, awaits further consideration

Therefore, the corresponding date for f. 1064 कात्तिके, शुक्लद्वादशी. मुडनाथ (सोम)बार is the 2nd November II42 A. D. Monday. The Nakshatra is Revati which is auspecious for महाद्वादशी according to the following verse:— For details see App. IV. 5. A king named Dharmakhedi was living in Kalinga under the Gangas as a प'चविपयाधिपति. There was matrimonial relationship of him with the Gangas of Kalinganagara. As he was a popular king, there is every possibility that a town in his name was established. Probably, Kuladitya (the donor) who is the lord of Dharmapura, belonged to the family of Udayaditya, the son of Dharmakhedi. (Vide Journal of the Bombay Hist-Society (March I93I) Vol IV, No I)

In S. 1067 the month तूल was ended before कार्तिक-शुक्ल-दशमी or two days before महाद्वादशी-The 12th tithi of the bright-half of Kartika in that year falls in Monday, but not in thursday, as found in the record. Therefore, I think, the date is not S. I067. But, in S. I068 the estronomical combination, as given in the inscription, fits well. Accordingly, I think, the corresponding date of this record is the 17th October. II46 A. D., Thursday. For महाद्वादशी see notes in No. I96, above

The grant is made for the occasion of महाव्यतीपात which occurred in the month of कुम्भ in अमावास्या and Sundy. It is again said to be a grant made for गङ्गास्नान. It is interesting to note here that the temple of Mukla-lingam was provided with some services for dancing, singing and drumming which were performed by the ' Deva-ganikas ' or the " Deva-dasis ". These duties were performed by both males and females of a selected family. 'The Indian music, according to the sastras, is only complete when dancing, singing and drumming were simultaneously performed:- (Vide the Sangītaratnākara) (Vide the Sangītadarpaṣa) (Vide the Sangīta Nārāyaṇa Vr. 12.)

D. when the Bhadrapada-Sukla-Dvadasi or the commencement of the Anka-year occurred. So, he must have ascended the thron some time between the 8th Sep. 1147 A. D. and the 20th Auguet, 1146 A. D. cells.remarks: † It is on a pillar to the left of the first entrance to the central shrine in the temple of Sri Kurmam. 2. Purnakoti (पूर्णकोटि) seems to be the old name of Sri Kurma. It is interesting to note here that near the Almora hill in the Himalayan range there is a mountain called the Kumaun, formally named as the Kurmachala (कूर्माचल). The tradition goes that the कूर्म श्रवतार of Vishnu was taken place in that locality. In 1849 Major Madden of Bengal Artillery's touring report was published in J. A. S. B. Vol. XVII, where at page 580 he refers to the Koormachal (कूर्माचल) with quotations from the स्कन्दपुताय. According to Major Madden, the name 'Koomas' was derived from 'Kurma' and it was identified with the modern मन्दारगिरि. In this connection Nundo Lal Dey says that "the celibrated temple of पूर्णदेवी or अन्नपूर्ण at पूर्णगिरि, visited by the pilgrims from all parts of the country; is situated in Kurmam". (Vide Hist. Geog. P. 106). Here also we find the god Kurmasvami at the place named पूर्णकोटि-पूर्णगिरि was a centre of the Tantric cult. Therefore, it awaits further study

In the note to No. 206 above I have shown that Kamarnava, Chodaganga's son, started his own srahi (Anka) in between 1146—7 A-D. (i. e. S. Io68-Io69). It is, therefore, presumed that Chodaganga died during the above period. So there is no necessity in using the Anka year of a king who was no more on the throne or even living. But, in spite of that we find that this record gives the Anka year of Chodaganga, about three years after he expired. This problem awaits further light

cells.remarks: * It is on the second pillar in the right row, south face, of the temple of Madhukesvara. 1. Kamārnava is the same as Madhukamārnava in No. 228 above. According to the Singhalese Chronicle , there lived a king named Vijayabāhu in Cylone who ruled from 1054 - 1109 A. D. It is known that he migrated from Simhapura of Kalinga, which was situated in the district of Kanyakubaia. identified with either Kannayabhadra or Kannayapeta of Parlakimedi taluk in the district of Ganjam. Vijayabāhu's queen Tril-kasundari was a daughter of the king of Kalinga. According to the Mahavrmsa ( 59, 46 ) three relatives of her. one of whom was named Madhukārnava, came to Cylone from Sihanura. Dr Hultzsch remarks that "the name Madhukārnava reminds us of the E. Gaṅga king Madhukamārnava" J. R. A. S. '913, P 520 f. n.). As Madhukāmārnavadeva, father of Vajrahasta III, died on or before §. 960 (1038 A. D.), there was no possibility for him to go to Cylone in the time of Vijayabāhu I. Therefore, Madhukāmārnava of the Singhalese Chronicle must be the King who succeeded Chodagaṅgadeva. This evidence, may not grind us to identify the donor of this grant with either the father of Vajrahasta III or the son of Chodagaṅga who ascended the throne of Kalinga in §. 1070 or 1148 A. D. 2. It is a gift made by Māsamadevi, queen of Kāmārnavadeva whose Abhisheka took place in Ś. 1065 when his father was living. The date of the present grant is gone. So, we have to depend upon the estronomical factors to fix up its date. The grant was issued on the Simha (Sankranti) and in Friday. According to the Indian Ephemeris of Swamikannu Pillai, the Simha Sankranti, between the Śaka years 1064 and 1078, falls in Śaka 1072 which corresponds to the 28th July, 1150 A. D. Printed by Sri A. T. Sarma, at the Siromani Press, Berhampur. 1960 I
